resumen: This/these point to things that are near (es: este, estos), and that/those point to things that are far (es: ese, aquel; esos, aquellos). They can go before a noun or alone, as pronouns.

explicacion.texto: English has only two distances: near and far. The Spanish “ese” and “aquel” are both that in English. The demonstrative agrees in number with the noun: this book, these books.

items: They are also used for time: this week (the week we are in now), that day (a day in the past), these days (nowadays).
On the phone: Hello, this is Marta (es: “Hola, soy Marta”).
To introduce someone: This is my friend Tom.
That's right / That's great: that refers to what someone has just said.

ejemplos.frase: Who are those people over there?
Mum, this is my teacher, Mr Smith.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mamá, te presento a mi profesor, el señor Smith.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: On the phone, you say who you are with this is.

ejercicios.explicacion: Look at the table on the card: for things that are near, this in the singular and these in the plural. The clue is apples, which is plural (and the verb are confirms it). So: These apples (es: “estas manzanas”).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Apples is plural and near: these.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is singular; apples is plural, so you need these.
Those is plural, but it is for things that are far; the instruction asks for the near form.

ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives that for one thing that is far. The clues are over there, which shows distance, and mountain, which is singular. In English that is used for both the Spanish “esa” and “aquella”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Mountain is singular and far: that.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Those is plural; mountain is singular, so that.
This is for things that are near; over there shows distance.

ejercicios.frase: Can you see ___ birds on the roof?
ejercicios.explicacion: Look at the row for far, plural, in the table: those. The clue is birds, which is plural, and on the roof, which is at some distance. Those is the Spanish “esos” or “aquellos”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Birds is plural and far: those.

errores_previstos.explicacion: That is singular; birds is plural and needs those.
These is for things that are near; the instruction asks for the far form.

ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives this for one thing that is near. The clue is seat, which is singular, and the context: we are asking about the seat next to us. So: Is this seat free?
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Seat is singular and near: this.

errores_previstos.explicacion: These is plural; seat is singular, so this.
That is for things that are far; when you ask about a free seat, it is usually next to you.

ejercicios.explicacion: The list on the card reminds you that demonstratives are also used for time: this week is the current week. The clue is week, which is singular, and the present tense I'm busy, which places the sentence now.

por_opcion.this: Correct: this week = the current week.
por_opcion.these: Incorrect: these is plural; with week it would be these weeks.
por_opcion.those: Incorrect: those is plural and far; it does not go with a singular noun or with the present.

ejercicios.frase: ___ jeans are too small for me.
ejercicios.explicacion: Remember number agreement from the card: the demonstrative is plural if the noun is plural. Jeans is always plural in English (like trousers or glasses), and the verb are confirms it. So: These jeans.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estos vaqueros me quedan demasiado pequeños.

por_opcion.This: Incorrect: this is singular, and jeans is plural in English, even though it is one item of clothing.
por_opcion.These: Correct: plural and near; it agrees with jeans.
por_opcion.That: Incorrect: that is singular and far.

ejercicios.frase: Hi, Paul. ___ is my cousin, Elena.
ejercicios.explicacion: The list on the card says that you use This is… to introduce someone. The clue is that you are introducing only one person (my cousin), so the singular this is correct.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To introduce one person: This is…
ejercicios.traduccion: Hola, Paul. Esta es mi prima, Elena.

por_opcion.This: Correct: This is… is the phrase to introduce one person.
por_opcion.These: Incorrect: these is plural; you use it to introduce several people (These are my cousins).
por_opcion.Those: Incorrect: those is plural and far; it is not used to introduce people.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card says that that is also used for things far away in time: that day = a day in the past (es: “aquel día”). The clue is in 2010, a moment far back in the past. This day would refer to today.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A moment far back in the past: that.

por_opcion.this: Incorrect: this day refers to the present; the day in 2010 is far back in time.
por_opcion.that: Correct: that for a moment far back in the past.
por_opcion.these: Incorrect: these is plural; day is singular.

ejercicios.explicacion: Remember agreement from the card: in the plural, this becomes these, the verb is becomes are and pen becomes pens. All the parts change at the same time.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: This is becomes these are, and pen becomes pens.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is singular; with are and pens you need these.
The noun also becomes plural: pens.
With these, the verb is plural: are.

ejercicios.explicacion: In the singular, those becomes that, houses becomes house and are becomes is. It is the same number agreement as on the card, in the other direction: when the number of the noun changes, the demonstrative and the verb change with it.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Those becomes that, and are becomes is.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The noun and the verb must also become singular: That house is old.
This is for things that are near; the singular of those is that.
With a singular subject, the verb is is.

ejercicios.explicacion: This is the first typical mistake on the card: this with a plural noun. Shoes is plural (and the verb are confirms it), so the demonstrative must be these. The rest of the sentence is already correct.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: this is singular and shoes is plural.
Making shoe singular leaves the verb are without agreement; you only need to change this to these.

ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives that for one thing that is far and those for the plural. Man is singular (the plural is men) and so is the verb is, so you must say that man.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: those is plural and man is singular.
Man is still singular; the correct form is Who is that man?

ejercicios.enunciado: Put the words in order to make a question.
ejercicios.explicacion: To ask about a price, use How much + be + object. Glasses (es: gafas) is always plural in English, so it goes with those and the verb are. Those shows that the glasses are at some distance, for example in the shop window.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: How much + are + those + plural noun.

errores_previstos.explicacion: That is the order of an indirect question; in a direct question the verb comes first: How much are those glasses?
The demonstrative goes before the noun: those glasses.

ejercicios.explicacion: Here this is a pronoun followed by is and a complement: This is my favourite room. This room is my favourite is also correct, with this as a determiner of room. In both cases this agrees with room in the singular.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The possessive and the adjective go before the noun: my favourite room.
The demonstrative goes before the noun: this room, not room this.
It is a question (“is this my favourite room?”), which makes no sense about your own tastes; the exercise asks for the statement: This is my favourite room.

descripcion_larga_es: The demonstratives this, that, these and those point to people or things depending on whether they are near or far, and whether there is one or more than one. They are among the first words you learn, and they are used all the time. They are difficult for Spanish speakers because English has only two distances (there is no difference between “ese” and “aquel”) and because the demonstrative changes in the plural, which is easy to forget.

contexto.que_es: They are words that point to something by its distance from the speaker. This (singular) and these (plural) for things that are near; that (singular) and those (plural) for things that are far. They can go before a noun (this book) or alone, as pronouns (This is my book).
contexto.por_que_importa: They are used all the time in shops, in introductions, on the phone and to refer to what someone has just said (That's right). Mixing up singular and plural (this books) is a very visible mistake, even if people still understand you. It appears in almost every basic-level exam.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When you point to things or people, introduce someone (This is my friend), say who you are on the phone (This is Marta) and in time expressions (this week, that day). The clue is the distance and the number of the noun. Spanish speakers tend to keep this with a plural noun and to translate “soy Marta” as I am Marta on the phone.
